summary: Checked 47 claims against the codebase, found 7 issues (0 critical, 3 major, 4 minor). All headline claims the caller asked about verified true: computeGroupClasses is order-agnostic, data-group-id sits on the group body and data-group-container is free, all four group-name display sites already receive group/board while EmptyState is the only one needing a new prop, BoardHeader is the sole consumer of both dataStore.updateBoard and BoardSettingsPopup.onSave, tsc currently fails with exactly two 'boardSettings.notes' errors, version 7 is hardcoded in exactly three source locations plus nine test expectations, and the project has no CI and no pre-commit hooks. The real problems are gaps rather than mirages: a required acceptance criterion (ellipsis truncation of long group titles) has no file assigned, the three-link onSave chain is split across two waves, and npx tsc --noEmit does not type-check .svelte files at all, making several per-task verification gates vacuous.

findings.claim: Task 5 'Group title display' modifies GroupHeader.svelte, CollapsibleGroup.svelte, GroupSettingsPopup.svelte, EmptyState.svelte, TaskGroup.svelte — src/styles.css is not listed in any task for group-title overflow handling.
findings.reality: User-spec AC (0011-feat-group-customization.md:165) requires: 'в заголовке группы на доске усекается многоточием'. src/styles.css:135-139 (.tm-group-header__title) and :219-221 (.tm-collapsible-group__title) have no overflow, text-overflow or min-width:0 — grep 'text-overflow' in src/styles.css hits only lines 423, 432, 591, 877, none of them a group title. The parent flex containers (.tm-group-header :125-131, .tm-collapsible-group__header :195-206) also lack min-width:0. The only tasks that list src/styles.css are Task 7 (grid order) and Task 8 (popup layout), neither of which describes title truncation.
findings.fix: Add src/styles.css to Task 5's 'Files to modify' and name the truncation work in its description — or move the truncation explicitly into Task 7, which already owns src/styles.css in the same wave. Note that Task 5 and Task 7 are both in Wave 2, so adding styles.css to Task 5 creates a same-wave write conflict on that file; assigning it to Task 7 is the safer option.

findings.claim: Backward Compatibility: 'BoardSettingsPopup's onSave signature grows; its only consumer is BoardHeader.svelte' — Task 6 (Wave 2) modifies src/stores/dataStore.ts and src/ui/BoardHeader.svelte, with src/ui/BoardSettingsPopup.svelte listed only as 'Files to read'; the popup itself is changed in Task 8 (Wave 3).
findings.reality: The save chain has three links that must change together: BoardSettingsPopup.svelte:8 declares the onSave prop type and :26 builds the fields object; BoardHeader.svelte:23-29 re-shapes it (fullWidths -> groupFullWidths) and calls updateBoard; dataStore.ts:199-214 writes the fields. The code-research this spec is built on states the same ('Цепочка onSave — три сигнатуры ... Все три придётся расширить одинаково'). Splitting them across waves means that after Wave 2 the popup still emits the old five-field object, so updateBoard writes undefined into board.groupOrder / group titles — while Task 7 (also Wave 2) has already made BoardLayout depend on board.groupOrder. Task 6's verify (npm test, npx tsc --noEmit) cannot catch this because no unit test covers the Svelte save path and tsc does not read .svelte files (see the separate finding).
findings.source: 0011-feat-group-customization-tech-spec.md, Backward Compatibility (Consumer impact) and Implementation Tasks, Task 6 vs Task 8
findings.fix: Either move the onSave signature extension in BoardSettingsPopup.svelte into Task 6 (declaration and pass-through only, leaving the UI controls to Task 8), or make Task 6 defensive: updateBoard should ignore/skip absent groupOrder and title fields rather than assign undefined.

findings.claim: Per-task verification table: Task 5 'verify: bash — npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build'; Decision 8: 'no task could pass a type-check gate'; Acceptance Criteria: 'npx tsc --noEmit is clean'.
findings.reality: npx tsc --noEmit does not type-check .svelte files in this project. tsconfig.json:17 lists 'src/**/*.svelte' in include, but tsc only compiles .ts/.tsx/.d.ts and silently ignores the rest — proof: src/ui/BoardSettingsPopup.svelte:90 calls $t('boardSettings.notes') with a key absent from the TranslationKey union, yet the current run reports only two errors, both in src/i18n/en.ts:60 and src/i18n/ru.ts:60. npm run build (esbuild + esbuild-svelte) does not type-check either. Task 5 modifies five .svelte files and nothing else, so its stated gate verifies nothing about the code it changes; the same applies to Task 7 (BoardLayout.svelte + styles.css) and Task 8.
findings.source: 0011-feat-group-customization-tech-spec.md, Agent Verification Plan (Per-task verification, rows 3/5/6) and Decision 8
findings.fix: Either add svelte-check (npx svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json) as the real gate for .svelte-only tasks, or restate the verification honestly: for Task 5 the meaningful gate is npm run build (compiles Svelte, catches syntax/prop errors) plus the E2E scenarios in Task 10, not tsc.

findings.claim: Solution: 'computeGroupClasses is already order-agnostic and needs no change'; Dependencies: 'src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts — computeGroupClasses, reused unchanged'.
findings.reality: Functionally correct — src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts:5-26 iterates the array it is given and pairs adjacent non-fullWidth entries, so any order works. But lines 3-4 of the same file carry a contract comment saying the opposite: 'ВАЖНО: зависит от фиксированного порядка групп. При появлении настраиваемого порядка — переработать.' No task lists src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts for modification, so the file ships with a comment that directly contradicts the shipped behavior and will mislead the next reader.
findings.fix: Add src/ui/boardLayoutUtils.ts to Task 7's 'Files to modify' with a one-line instruction to update or delete the stale comment (the function body stays untouched).

findings.claim: Decision 7: 'Add engines to package.json and an .nvmrc requiring Node >= 22.12 ... The requirement is the intersection of what the build tooling and package manager need.'
findings.reality: The floor is safe but is not the intersection. Actual declared engines: vite 7.3.1 -> '^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0'; vitest 4.0.18 -> '^20.0.0 || ^22.0.0 || >=24.0.0'; npm 11.13 warns it supports '^20.17.0 || >=22.9.0'. The intersection is '^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0' — Node 20.19+ satisfies every constraint. Current environment is Node v18.19.1, and npm test indeed fails there with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM inside vite's config loader, which matches the require(ESM) availability boundary (20.19 / 22.12).
findings.fix: State it as a deliberate choice ('we pin >=22.12 rather than the full ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0 range'), or write the real range into engines.node so a developer on Node 20.19+ is not blocked by Task 2's runtime precondition check.

findings.claim: Task 5 description: 'Show the user-defined name everywhere a group name appears — board header, collapsed header, the group's own settings popup and the board settings list'.
findings.reality: The board settings list is src/ui/BoardSettingsPopup.svelte:61 ({$groupLabels[groupId]}), which is not in Task 5's 'Files to modify' — it appears only in Task 8 (Wave 3), where the label is replaced by a text input. The description and the file list disagree about what Task 5 delivers.
findings.fix: Drop 'and the board settings list' from Task 5's description and note there that the popup row is covered by Task 8.

findings.claim: Backward Compatibility: 'Sanitization runs on every load, not only during migration, so data damaged later is repaired too.'
findings.reality: migrateData is indeed invoked on every load (src/main.ts:52, this.data = migrateData(raw)), so the entry point supports the claim. But every existing step in src/data/migration.ts:19-82 is wrapped in an 'if (version < N)' guard; delivering unconditional sanitization requires a block outside those guards, and neither Decision 6 nor Task 1's description says so explicitly. Decision 6 attributes the sanitization to migrateData without stating it must be unguarded.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to Task 1: the groupOrder sanitization must sit outside every 'if (version < N)' guard so it runs on every load, and cover it with a unit test that feeds already-v8 data with a damaged groupOrder.
